content.content:
1	"""Portable offline export of a saved split plan.
2	
3	An export package is a self-contained ZIP: one directory per set
4	(``train``/``validation``/``test``), each containing the same numbered
5	ImageFolder class directories, plus a UTF-8 JSON manifest.  Samples are
6	stored under ``<set>/<class>/<full-sha256><source-extension>``.
7	
8	The export is driven solely by the saved plan: its sample identities,
9	labels, set assignments and recorded source paths.  Later imports, label
10	changes or undos never affect an exported package, and exporting never
11	writes to the workspace.
12	
13	Without ``source_dir`` each sample is copied from its recorded source
14	path.  A path that is a symbolic link when the export starts is followed
15	once, exactly like a single-file import, and the regular file the link
16	then names is the object confirmed for this read.  From that point the
17	read is pinned with the same inspect / open-no-follow / fstat-prove rule
18	as a source-directory copy: the concrete target is lstat()ed, opened with
19	``O_NOFOLLOW`` plus ``O_NONBLOCK`` and proved by descriptor to be that
20	exact regular file.  Another regular file renamed onto the path in the
21	gap — even one with identical content, size and modification time — is
22	rejected as a replaced source rather than read, and a named pipe swapped
23	into the gap (even with no writer) is opened without blocking and then
24	rejected, so the export neither waits for data nor packages pipe bytes.
25	Failures name the sample's full digest, the recorded source path and the
26	reason; the recorded path is never rewritten and no same-content
27	replacement is substituted.
28	
29	When ``source_dir`` is given, files are read from that directory tree
30	instead of the recorded source paths: every regular file under the
31	directory (no extension filter; symlinks and other non-regular entries
32	are skipped and symlinked directories are never descended) is read in
33	full and identified by content digest, and each exported sample is
34	matched to a file whose full SHA-256 matches the plan.  Each scan read
35	is itself pinned with the same inspect / open-no-follow-nonblocking /
36	fstat-prove rule as the package copy: the exact regular file the walk
37	typed is the object whose bytes are hashed, so a named pipe swapped
38	into the gap before the lookup read — even one with no writer, or one
39	whose writer would supply the planned bytes — is opened without
40	blocking and rejected before any byte is consumed, and another
41	regular file landing there (even byte-, size- and mtime-identical) is
42	rejected the same way.  The selected copy is pinned again through the
43	open when it is streamed into the package (lstat without symlink
44	follow, ``O_NOFOLLOW`` and an fstat of the descriptor), so the bytes
45	read come from the exact regular file confirmed at lookup time; a
46	replacement landing after the lookup — another regular file, even
47	with identical content, or a symlink, even pointing at the original
48	file — fails the export.
49	
50	The walk itself is anchored to directory descriptors: the confirmed
51	root is held open for the whole export and each directory is entered
52	with ``openat`` (``O_NOFOLLOW`` plus ``O_DIRECTORY``) relative to its
53	parent's descriptor and verified with ``fstatat`` on both the
54	parent-relative name and the opened descriptor, so a real subdirectory
55	cannot be followed through even if its path is swapped for a symlink in
56	the gap between its first inspection and its entry.  A subdirectory
57	confirmed real during the walk that is a symlink by the time it is
58	entered — whether the link points outside the tree, inside it, or at
59	the moved original — fails the whole export naming that path and the
60	symlink; the same applies to a swap landing while its children are
61	being processed.
62	
63	The protection extends to the package copy that follows the lookup.
64	Before each matched file is opened its ancestor directories are
65	re-derived and re-pinned through the same descriptor-anchored checks,
66	and after every sample has been streamed every directory recorded
67	during the walk is verified once more before the package is published:
68	a real directory replaced by a symlink after the lookup — before a
69	sample is opened, while a sample is read or between samples — still
70	fails the export, and a byte-equal file behind the new link is never
71	read, matched or packaged.  Entries that are symlinks when first
72	encountered keep being skipped exactly as before.
73	
74	The new directory only changes where bytes are read from; sample
75	identities, labels, set assignments and package file extensions remain
76	the plan's.  The lookup is used for this one export only and is never
77	written back.
78	
79	ZIP bytes are deterministic for a given plan, options and source content:
80	entry metadata uses fixed values, entries are written in a fixed order and
81	source modification times are never consulted.
82	
83	A single sample whose bytes reach the classic ZIP 32-bit size limit
84	(2 GiB, or close enough that its deflated form could) is written as a
85	ZIP64 entry: the local file header carries a ZIP64 extra field with the
86	real sizes while the entry is streamed, so no sample has to fit in
87	memory and highly compressible multi-gigabyte content is supported even
88	when the resulting package stays small.  Plans containing only smaller
89	samples use exactly the classic format they always did, byte for byte.
90	"""
91	
92	from __future__ import annotations
93	
94	import errno
95	import fcntl
96	import hashlib
97	import json
98	import os
99	import stat
100	import tempfile
101	import zipfile
102	from collections import Counter
103	from pathlib import Path
104	from typing import Any
105	
106	from . import confirmed
107	from .splits import SET_NAMES, SplitError, invalid_digest_reason
108	
109	EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1
110	
111	# Fixed ZIP entry metadata: deterministic across machines and runs.
112	_FIXED_DATE_TIME = (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
113	_CREATE_SYSTEM_UNIX = 3
114	_FILE_ATTR = 0o100644 << 16
115	_DIR_ATTR = (0o40755 << 16) | 0x10  # MS-DOS directory flag
116	_CHUNK_SIZE = 1024 * 1024
117	# Descriptor-relative, no-symlink-follow directory opens: POSIX and
118	# available on the platforms this tool runs on (0 where a flag is absent).
119	_O_NOFOLLOW = getattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW", 0)
120	_O_DIRECTORY = getattr(os, "O_DIRECTORY", 0)
121	
122	
123	class ExportError(ValueError):
124	    """An export cannot be produced."""
125	
126	
127	def _entry_needs_zip64(file_size: int) -> bool:
128	    """Whether one sample entry must use the ZIP64 local header.
129	
130	    Mirrors zipfile's own pre-streaming heuristic (the uncompressed size
131	    plus a 5% margin, compared with the 32-bit size field limit): the
132	    margin covers both a size landing at the exact limit and deflate
133	    growth past it on incompressible content, while everything below it
134	    keeps the classic header byte for byte.
135	    """
136	    return file_size * 21 > zipfile.ZIP64_LIMIT * 20
137	
138	
139	def export_split(
140	    store: Any,
141	    plan_name: str,
142	    target: Path,
143	    skip_unlabeled: bool = False,
144	    source_dir: Path | None = None,
145	) -> dict[str, Any]:
146	    """Export a saved split plan to a new ZIP at ``target``.
147	
148	    Returns a result payload describing the plan, the number of samples
149	    actually exported, the class distribution per set and the per-set skip
150	    counts.  Raises :class:`ExportError` (a ``ValueError``) on any failure;
151	    the target path is never created in that case.
152	
153	    When ``source_dir`` is given, sample bytes are read from that directory
154	    tree instead of the plan's recorded source paths: the directory is
155	    walked (regular files only, no extension filter, never through
156	    symlinks), every regular file is hashed in full, and each exported
157	    sample is matched to a file with the same full SHA-256 digest.  Both
158	    the lookup hashes and the later copy use the same pinned
159	    inspect/open/prove rule: a named pipe or a different regular file
160	    (even a byte-identical one) swapped in after a scan entry was typed
161	    fails the export before its bytes are read or waited on, just as a
162	    swap landing after the lookup does when the selected copy is opened.
163	    The plan still decides identities, labels, set assignments and
164	    package file extensions; the lookup is used for this export only.
165	
166	    Without ``source_dir`` each sample is read from its recorded source
167	    path, pinned to the one ordinary regular file confirmed immediately
168	    before the read: a symlink present at the start is followed once,
169	    while a replacement landing in the confirm-to-open gap — another
170	    regular file, even a byte-identical one, or a named pipe, even one
171	    with no writer — fails the whole export instead of being read.
172	
173	    The walk is anchored to directory descriptors, so a subdirectory that
174	    was a real directory when the walk reached it but has become a symlink
175	    before it is entered or while its contents are read fails the export
176	    naming that path; the link is never followed.
177	    """
178	    try:
179	        plan = store.get_split(plan_name)
180	    except SplitError as error:
181	        # Reading a saved plan already enforces the same identity and
182	        # proportion rules as "split show"; export reports them through
183	        # its own error type while keeping the message (plan name, set,
184	        # member position and the concrete problem) intact.  This runs
185	        # before the unlabeled check, so --skip-unlabeled can never
186	        # bypass a corrupted identity.
187	        raise ExportError(str(error)) from error
188	    members = _collect_members(plan)
189	
190	    unlabeled = [member for member in members if member["label"] == ""]
191	    if unlabeled and not skip_unlabeled:
192	        first = min(unlabeled, key=lambda member: member["sha256"])
193	        raise ExportError(
194	            f"sample {first['sha256']} in set {first['set']} has no label; "
195	            "pass --skip-unlabeled to export without unlabeled samples"
196	        )
197	
198	    exported = [member for member in members if member["label"] != ""]
199	    skipped_counts = {set_name: 0 for set_name in SET_NAMES}
200	    for member in unlabeled:
201	        skipped_counts[member["set"]] += 1
202	
203	    classes = _build_classes(exported)
204	    manifest = _build_manifest(plan, classes, exported, skipped_counts)
205	    distributions = _distributions(exported)
206	
207	    resolver = None
208	    if source_dir is not None:
209	        source_dir = Path(source_dir)
210	        if not source_dir.exists():
211	            raise ExportError(f"source directory does not exist: {source_dir}")
212	        if not source_dir.is_dir():
213	            raise ExportError(f"source is not a directory: {source_dir}")
214	        # An empty plan (or every sample skipped) needs no files at all;
215	        # the directory still has to exist and be one.
216	        if exported:
217	            resolved_root = source_dir.resolve()
218	            # Keep the confirmed root open and pinned for the whole
219	            # export: the lookup and the later package copy both resolve
220	            # through this descriptor, so a subdirectory turned into a
221	            # symlink after the lookup cannot be traversed while reading
222	            # the package bytes either.
223	            try:
224	                root_fd = os.open(resolved_root, os.O_RDONLY | _O_DIRECTORY)
225	            except OSError as error:
226	                raise ExportError(
227	                    f"cannot scan directory {resolved_root}: {error}"
228	                ) from error
229	            try:
230	                resolver = _scan_source_directory(resolved_root)
231	                for member in exported:
232	                    if member["sha256"] not in resolver:
233	                        raise ExportError(
234	                            f"sample {member['sha256']} in set {member['set']}: "
235	                            f"no file with matching content (full SHA-256 "
236	                            f"{member['sha256']}) found under source directory "
237	                            f"{source_dir}"
238	                        )
239	                directory_ids = getattr(resolver, "directory_ids", None)
240	                anchor = (
241	                    _SourceAnchor(root_fd, resolved_root, directory_ids)
242	                    if directory_ids is not None
243	                    else None
244	                )
245	                _write_package(
246	                    target,
247	                    classes,
248	                    exported,
249	                    manifest,
250	                    resolver,
251	                    source_anchor=anchor,
252	                )
253	            finally:
254	                os.close(root_fd)
255	        else:
256	            _write_package(target, classes, exported, manifest, None)
257	    else:
258	        _write_package(target, classes, exported, manifest, None)
259	
260	    return {
261	        "plan": plan["name"],
262	        "exported": len(exported),
263	        "skipped": skipped_counts,
264	        "sets": {
265	            set_name: {
266	                "samples": distributions[set_name]["samples"],
267	                "distribution": dict(
268	                    sorted(distributions[set_name]["distribution"].items())
269	                ),
270	            }
271	            for set_name in SET_NAMES
272	        },
273	        "target": str(target.resolve()),
274	    }

277	def _collect_members(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
278	    """Flatten plan members and validate the fields export depends on."""
279	    members: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
280	    for set_name in SET_NAMES:
281	        payload = plan["sets"][set_name]
282	        for position, member in enumerate(payload["members"], start=1):
283	            digest = member.get("sha256")
284	            label = member.get("label")
285	            source = member.get("source")
286	            digest_problem = invalid_digest_reason(digest)
287	            if digest_problem is not None:
288	                raise ExportError(
289	                    f"split plan {plan.get('name')!r} is corrupted: "
290	                    f"{set_name} member {position} has an invalid 'sha256' "
291	                    f"identity {digest!r}: {digest_problem}"
292	                )
293	            if not isinstance(label, str):
294	                raise ExportError(
295	                    f"split plan {plan.get('name')!r} is corrupted: "
296	                    f"{set_name} member {position} (sha256 {digest}) has a "
297	                    "non-string label"
298	                )
299	            if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
300	                raise ExportError(
301	                    f"split plan {plan.get('name')!r} is corrupted: "
302	                    f"{set_name} member {position} (sha256 {digest}) has no "
303	                    "recorded source path"
304	                )
305	            members.append(
306	                {
307	                    "sha256": digest,
308	                    "label": label,
309	                    "source": source,
310	                    "set": set_name,
311	                }
312	            )
313	    return members
314	
315	
316	def _build_classes(members: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, str]:
317	    """Map every exported label to one shared numbered class directory.
318	
319	    All sets use the same numbering; labels are sorted by their literal
320	    text so Chinese labels, labels containing path separators and labels
321	    differing only in case each get a distinct, collision-free directory.
322	    """
323	    labels = sorted({member["label"] for member in members})
324	    width = max(2, len(str(len(labels)))) if labels else 2
325	    return {label: f"class_{index:0{width}d}" for index, label in enumerate(labels, 1)}
326	
327	
328	def _build_manifest(
329	    plan: dict[str, Any],
330	    classes: dict[str, str],
331	    members: list[dict[str, Any]],
332	    skipped_counts: dict[str, int],
333	) -> dict[str, Any]:
334	    set_summaries = {}
335	    for set_name in SET_NAMES:
336	        set_members = [member for member in members if member["set"] == set_name]
337	        set_summaries[set_name] = {
338	            "samples": len(set_members),
339	            "skipped": skipped_counts[set_name],
340	        }
341	
342	    sample_entries = []
343	    for member in sorted(members, key=lambda item: item["sha256"]):
344	        arc_path = _sample_path(member, classes[member["label"]])
345	        sample_entries.append(
346	            {
347	                "sha256": member["sha256"],
348	                "label": member["label"],
349	                "set": member["set"],
350	                "path": arc_path,
351	            }
352	        )
353	
354	    return {
355	        "schema_version": EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION,
356	        "plan": plan["name"],
357	        "seed": plan["seed"],
358	        "ratios": {set_name: plan["ratios"][set_name] for set_name in SET_NAMES},
359	        "classes": [
360	            {"label": label, "directory": directory}
361	            for label, directory in sorted(classes.items())
362	        ],
363	        "sets": set_summaries,
364	        "samples": sample_entries,
365	    }
366	
367	
368	def _sample_path(member: dict[str, Any], class_directory: str) -> str:
369	    """Package-relative path for a sample: ``<set>/<class>/<digest><ext>``."""
370	    extension = Path(member["source"]).suffix
371	    return f"{member['set']}/{class_directory}/{member['sha256']}{extension}"
372	
373	
374	def _distributions(members: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
375	    result: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
376	    for set_name in SET_NAMES:
377	        set_members = [member for member in members if member["set"] == set_name]
378	        result[set_name] = {
379	            "samples": len(set_members),
380	            "distribution": Counter(member["label"] for member in set_members),
381	        }
382	    return result
383	
384	
385	# A resolver maps a full SHA-256 digest to the absolute path of the
386	# sorted-first regular file carrying that content, plus the file's
387	# identity (device, inode) of the proved object actually hashed during
388	# the lookup.  The copy opens that exact inode pinned through the open,
389	# so a swap after the lookup — another regular file, even with
390	# identical content, or a symlink, even one pointing at the original
391	# file — cannot be read in its place; swaps landing in the gap inside
392	# the lookup itself are rejected by the scan before the digest is
393	# recorded.
394	Resolver = dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]]
395	
396	
397	class _ScanResult(dict):
398	    """The digest resolver, also carrying every real directory seen.
399	
400	    Behaves as the plain digest-to-file resolver mapping, with an extra
401	    ``directory_ids`` attribute: each key is a ``/``-separated path

415	def _scan_source_directory(root: Path) -> Resolver:
416	    """Walk ``root`` and map every digest to the sorted-first copy.
417	
418	    The directory and all its subdirectories are searched for regular
419	    files only: there is no extension filter, symlinks and other
420	    non-regular entries are skipped, and recursion never descends through
421	    symlinked directories.  Every regular file found is read in full and
422	    identified by its content digest; when several files share content,
423	    the one whose slash-separated path relative to ``root`` sorts first
424	    by Unicode code point owns the digest.  A directory that cannot be
425	    scanned, an entry that cannot be inspected or a file that cannot be
426	    read in full fails the export with the path and reason.
427	
428	    Each file read is itself pinned through the shared
429	    inspect / open-no-follow-with-nonblocking / fstat-prove rule: the
430	    bytes hashed come from the exact regular file the walk typed, and
431	    an object swapped onto the name in that gap — a named pipe (even
432	    with no writer), a symlink or another regular file, even a
433	    byte-identical one — fails the export before any of its bytes are
434	    read, naming the path and what it became.
435	
436	    Every step is anchored to directory descriptors rather than path
437	    strings: a child is typed and entered with ``fstatat``/``openat``
438	    relative to the descriptor of the directory it was listed from, and
439	    each entered directory is pinned for the whole time its contents are
440	    processed.  A real subdirectory whose path is swapped for a symlink
441	    after it was listed but before or while it is entered therefore can
442	    never be followed — the open refuses the link and the export fails
443	    naming that directory — and a swap landing while its children are
444	    being read is detected when its path binding is re-checked after the
445	    children have been processed.  Only entries that are already
446	    symlinks when first listed are skipped, preserving the original
447	    convention.
448	    """
449	    try:
450	        root_fd = os.open(root, os.O_RDONLY | _O_DIRECTORY)
451	    except OSError as error:
452	        raise ExportError(f"cannot scan directory {root}: {error}") from error
453	    try:
454	        return _scan_tree(root_fd, root)
455	    finally:
456	        os.close(root_fd)

459	def _scan_tree(root_fd: int, root: Path) -> _ScanResult:
460	    """Walk the tree reached through the already-open, pinned ``root_fd``."""
461	    found: dict[str, tuple[str, Path, int, int]] = {}
462	    directories: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]] = {}
463	    try:
464	        root_status = os.fstat(root_fd)
465	    except OSError as error:
466	        raise ExportError(f"cannot scan directory {root}: {error}") from error
467	    directories[""] = (root, root_status.st_dev, root_status.st_ino)
468	    _walk_directory(root_fd, None, root, root, found, directories)
469	    files = {
470	        digest: (path, device, inode)
471	        for digest, (_, path, device, inode) in found.items()
472	    }
473	    return _ScanResult(files, directories)

476	def _walk_directory(
477	    parent_fd: int,
478	    name: str | None,
479	    display: Path,
480	    root: Path,
481	    found: dict[str, tuple[str, Path, int, int]],
482	    directories: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]],
483	) -> None:
484	    """Process one directory, anchored to a pinned descriptor.
485	
486	    ``name`` is the parent-relative basename; ``None`` marks the already
487	    open ``root`` whose descriptor is ``parent_fd``.  Any other
488	    directory is entered through :func:`_enter_subdirectory`, which
489	    pins the exact directory listed by the parent.
490	    """
491	    if name is None:
492	        directory_fd = parent_fd
493	        entered = False
494	    else:
495	        directory_fd = _enter_subdirectory(parent_fd, name, display)
496	        entered = True
497	    try:
498	        if entered:
499	            try:
500	                pinned = os.fstat(directory_fd)
501	            except OSError as error:
502	                raise ExportError(
503	                    f"cannot scan directory {display}: {error}"
504	                ) from error
505	            rel = os.path.relpath(display, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
506	            directories[rel] = (display, pinned.st_dev, pinned.st_ino)
507	        try:
508	            entries = list(os.scandir(directory_fd))
509	        except OSError as error:
510	            raise ExportError(f"cannot scan directory {display}: {error}") from error
511	        for entry in entries:
512	            child_name = entry.name
513	            child_display = display / child_name
514	            try:
515	                status = os.stat(
516	                    child_name, dir_fd=directory_fd, follow_symlinks=False
517	                )
518	            except OSError as error:
519	                raise ExportError(
520	                    f"cannot inspect entry {child_display}: {error}"
521	                ) from error
522	            mode = status.st_mode
523	            if stat.S_ISLNK(mode):
524	                # A symlink when first encountered: skipped, never read.
525	                continue
526	            if stat.S_ISREG(mode):
527	                digest, device, inode = _hash_regular_file_at(
528	                    directory_fd, child_name, child_display
529	                )
530	                rel = os.path.relpath(child_display, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
531	                current = found.get(digest)
532	                if current is None or rel < current[0]:
533	                    found[digest] = (rel, child_display, device, inode)
534	            elif stat.S_ISDIR(mode):
535	                _walk_directory(
536	                    directory_fd,
537	                    child_name,
538	                    child_display,
539	                    root,
540	                    found,
541	                    directories,
542	                )
543	            # Any other entry type is skipped as before.
544	        if entered:
545	            # The children are done and were all reached through this
546	            # pinned descriptor.  Re-prove the parent-relative name still
547	            # binds to this same directory: a symlink (or anything else)
548	            # swapped onto it while the children were being processed
549	            # must fail the export even though nothing was read through
550	            # that link.
551	            _assert_still_same_directory(
552	                parent_fd, name, display, directory_fd
553	            )
554	    finally:
555	        if entered:
556	            os.close(directory_fd)

559	def _enter_subdirectory(parent_fd: int, name: str, display: Path) -> int:
560	    """Open a listed subdirectory relative to ``parent_fd`` and pin it.
561	
562	    The parent listed ``name`` as a real directory, so anything other
563	    than that same directory observed here means the path changed after
564	    the listing.  This is the first confirmation of the directory: no
565	    identity was recorded yet, so the fresh inspection itself sets the
566	    expectation the opened descriptor is then proved against.  A symlink
567	    swapped in at any point fails the export identifying ``display`` as
568	    a directory that changed into a symlink, and its target — outside
569	    the tree, inside it, or the moved original — is never touched.
570	    """
571	    return _open_confirmed_directory(
572	        parent_fd, name, display, expected=None, during_scan=True
573	    )

576	def _open_confirmed_directory(
577	    parent_fd: int,
578	    name: str,
579	    display: Path,
580	    expected: tuple[int, int] | None,
581	    during_scan: bool,
582	) -> int:
583	    """Open ``name`` relative to ``parent_fd`` and pin the directory.
584	
585	    The single confirmation rule shared by the lookup and the package
586	    copy: the name is inspected with ``fstatat`` without following
587	    symlinks and then opened with ``openat`` using ``O_NOFOLLOW`` and
588	    ``O_DIRECTORY``; the descriptor is fstat()ed and proved to be the
589	    directory the inspection named.  ``expected`` carries the
590	    ``(device, inode)`` the binding must match — the identity recorded
591	    during the lookup when the copy re-checks an already confirmed
592	    directory, or ``None`` when the lookup confirms a directory for the
593	    first time and the fresh inspection itself is the expectation.
594	
595	    ``during_scan`` selects the phase the error messages report:
596	    failures while walking the tree say "during scan" and "cannot scan",
597	    failures while copying the package say "during export" and "cannot
598	    inspect".  A symlink swapped in at any point in this sequence fails
599	    the export identifying ``display`` and what it became; the link's
600	    target is never touched.
601	    """
602	    try:
603	        before = os.stat(name, dir_fd=parent_fd, follow_symlinks=False)
604	    except OSError as error:
605	        raise ExportError(f"cannot inspect directory {display}: {error}") from error
606	    if expected is None:
607	        expected = (before.st_dev, before.st_ino)
608	    if (
609	        stat.S_ISLNK(before.st_mode)
610	        or not stat.S_ISDIR(before.st_mode)
611	        or (before.st_dev, before.st_ino) != expected
612	    ):
613	        raise _directory_changed_message(
614	            display, before.st_mode, during_scan=during_scan
615	        )
616	    try:
617	        descriptor = os.open(
618	            name,
619	            os.O_RDONLY | _O_NOFOLLOW | _O_DIRECTORY,
620	            dir_fd=parent_fd,
621	        )
622	    except OSError as error:
623	        if error.errno in (errno.ELOOP, errno.ENOTDIR):
624	            # The path changed between the fstatat and the open; inspect
625	            # it once more to report the concrete reason.
626	            raise _directory_changed_error(
627	                parent_fd, name, display, during_scan=during_scan
628	            ) from error
629	        raise _directory_access_error(display, error, during_scan) from error
630	    try:
631	        opened = os.fstat(descriptor)
632	    except OSError as error:
633	        os.close(descriptor)
634	        raise _directory_access_error(display, error, during_scan) from error
635	    if not stat.S_ISDIR(opened.st_mode) or (
636	        opened.st_dev,
637	        opened.st_ino,
638	    ) != expected:
639	        os.close(descriptor)
640	        raise _directory_changed_error(
641	            parent_fd, name, display, during_scan=during_scan
642	        )
643	    return descriptor

650	    action = "scan" if during_scan else "inspect"
651	    return ExportError(f"cannot {action} directory {display}: {error}")

684	def _directory_changed_message(
685	    display: Path, mode: int | None, during_scan: bool
686	) -> ExportError:

688	    phase = "during scan" if during_scan else "during export"

690	        reason = "is now a symlink"
691	    elif mode is not None and stat.S_ISDIR(mode):
692	        reason = "was replaced by a different directory"
693	    else:

695	    return ExportError(f"directory changed {phase}: {display} {reason}")

698	class _SourceAnchor:
699	    """Pinned view of the confirmed source tree, used while copying.
700	
701	    Holds the root descriptor for the whole export and the identity of
702	    every directory observed during the lookup.  Each verification
703	    re-derives directory bindings from descriptors (``fstatat`` and
704	    ``openat`` with ``O_NOFOLLOW``/``O_DIRECTORY``) instead of trusting
705	    path strings, so a real directory replaced by a symlink after the
706	    lookup — before a sample is opened, while it is read or between
707	    samples — fails the export even when the link leads to byte-equal
708	    content.  :meth:`verify_all` runs once more after every sample has
709	    been copied, so the package is never published when a binding
710	    changed.
711	    """
712	
713	    def __init__(
714	        self,
715	        root_fd: int,
716	        root: Path,
717	        directories: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]],
718	    ) -> None:
719	        self.root_fd = root_fd
720	        self.root = root
721	        self.directories = directories
722	
723	    def verify_file(self, source: Path) -> None:
724	        """Prove the root and all ancestor directories of ``source``."""
725	        parts = source.relative_to(self.root).parts[:-1]
726	        self._descend(tuple(parts))
727	
728	    def verify_all(self) -> None:
729	        """Prove the root and every directory recorded during the lookup.
730	
731	        A single descriptor-anchored traversal over the recorded
732	        parent/child structure opens each directory exactly once, so a
733	        tree of any depth costs one descent rather than one per
734	        directory.  Every open is an ``openat`` relative to the pinned
735	        parent, so a symlink swapped in at any level is refused.
736	        """
737	        self._check_root()
738	        children: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]] = {}
739	        for key in self.directories:
740	            if not key:
741	                continue
742	            parent_key, _, name = key.rpartition("/")
743	            children.setdefault(parent_key, []).append((name, key))
744	        self._verify_children(self.root_fd, "", self.root, children)
745	
746	    def _check_root(self) -> None:
747	        _, root_dev, root_inode = self.directories[""]
748	        try:
749	            pinned_root = os.fstat(self.root_fd)
750	        except OSError as error:
751	            raise ExportError(
752	                f"cannot inspect directory {self.root}: {error}"
753	            ) from error
754	        if (pinned_root.st_dev, pinned_root.st_ino) != (
755	            root_dev,
756	            root_inode,
757	        ) or not stat.S_ISDIR(pinned_root.st_mode):
758	            raise _directory_changed_message(
759	                self.root, pinned_root.st_mode, during_scan=False
760	            )
761	
762	    def _verify_children(
763	        self,
764	        parent_fd: int,
765	        parent_key: str,
766	        display: Path,
767	        children: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]],
768	    ) -> None:
769	        for name, key in sorted(children.get(parent_key, ())):
770	            child_display = display / name
771	            descriptor = self._open_checked(
772	                parent_fd, child_display.name, child_display,
773	                *self.directories[key][1:],
774	            )
775	            try:
776	                self._verify_children(
777	                    descriptor, key, child_display, children
778	                )
779	            finally:
780	                os.close(descriptor)

782	    def _descend(self, parts: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
783	        # Start from the root descriptor held open since before the
784	        # lookup: it pins the confirmed root inode regardless of later
785	        # path changes.  Only intermediate children are opened here, and
786	        # each is closed before returning (the root descriptor itself is
787	        # owned by the export and must not be closed).
788	        self._check_root()
789	        cursor = self.root_fd
790	        display = self.root
791	        owned: list[int] = []
792	        try:
793	            for part in parts:
794	                display = display / part
795	                key = os.path.relpath(display, self.root).replace(os.sep, "/")
796	                expected = self.directories.get(key)
797	                if expected is None:
798	                    raise ExportError(
799	                        f"directory changed during export: {display} is "
800	                        f"not part of the scanned tree"
801	                    )
802	                cursor = self._open_checked(cursor, part, display, *expected[1:])
803	                owned.append(cursor)
804	        finally:
805	            for descriptor in owned:
806	                os.close(descriptor)

836	
837	def _hash_regular_file_at(
838	    directory_fd: int, name: str, path: Path
839	) -> tuple[str, int, int]:
840	    """Read one directory-relative file in full, pinned through the open.
841	
842	    The name is inspected with ``fstatat`` relative to the pinned
843	    directory descriptor and the exact regular file confirmed there is
844	    then opened with ``openat`` plus ``O_NOFOLLOW`` and ``O_NONBLOCK``;
845	    the descriptor is fstat()ed and proved to be that same object
846	    before any byte is read.  Closing the inspect/open gap this way
847	    means an object swapped in after the walk typed the entry — a
848	    named pipe, even one with no writer or one whose writer would
849	    supply the planned bytes, a symlink, or another regular file, even
850	    one with identical content, size and modification time — fails the
851	    export immediately: the open never waits for a writer, the swapped
852	    object's bytes are never hashed, and the error names this path.
853	    The recorded identity is the proved descriptor's
854	    ``(device, inode)`` — the object the bytes actually came from —
855	    which the copy later independently re-pins before streaming the
856	    package.  Any failure raises with the path and reason.  Returns
857	    ``(digest, device, inode)``.
858	
859	    The confirm/open/prove rule and the chunked hashing come from
860	    :mod:`confirmed`, shared with import; only the export wording is
861	    assembled here.
862	    """
863	    try:
864	        confirmed_status = confirmed.inspect_regular(name, dir_fd=directory_fd)
865	        descriptor = confirmed.open_without_follow(name, dir_fd=directory_fd)
866	        # prove_opened_regular closes the descriptor on rejection; on
867	        # success it also clears the open's temporary O_NONBLOCK, so the
868	        # descriptor hash_descriptor streams is an ordinary blocking one.
869	        opened = confirmed.prove_opened_regular(descriptor, confirmed_status)
870	    except confirmed.ConfirmationError as failure:
871	        if failure.stage is confirmed.ConfirmStage.OPEN:
872	            raise _scan_open_error(
873	                failure, directory_fd, name, path, confirmed_status
874	            ) from failure
875	        raise _scan_file_error(failure, path) from failure
876	    try:
877	        digest = confirmed.hash_descriptor(descriptor)
878	    except OSError as error:
879	        raise ExportError(f"cannot read source file {path}: {error}") from error
880	    # The descriptor was proved to be the confirmed regular file, so
881	    # the identity the bytes carry is the opened object's own.
882	    return digest, opened.st_dev, opened.st_ino

950	
951	    The walk had just typed this name as a regular file, so a symlink,
952	    a named pipe or any other object that occupies it while the open is
953	    pinned is a source that changed before it was read: the export fails
954	    naming the path and the new occupant, without ever waiting on the
955	    object or hashing its bytes.  Entries that were already

970	        # regular file: the entry changed before the pinned open.

981	def _assert_target_name_free(target: Path) -> None:
982	    """Reject an occupied target name without following a final symlink.
983	
984	    ``lstat`` inspects the name itself, so a symlink counts as occupied
985	    even when it points at a location that does not exist.  Only a proven
986	    ``ENOENT`` means the name is free; any other inspection error fails
987	    the export too, rather than risking a write at a name that cannot be
988	    shown to be free.
989	    """
990	    try:
991	        os.lstat(target)
992	    except FileNotFoundError:
993	        return
994	    except OSError as error:
995	        raise ExportError(f"cannot inspect target {target}: {error}") from error
996	    raise ExportError(f"target already exists: {target}")

999	def _publish_package(temp_path: Path, target: Path) -> None:
1000	    """Publish the finished package without ever replacing the target name.
1001	
1002	    The package is complete and source-verified by the time this runs.
1003	    The name is re-checked and then claimed with a single ``link(2)``,
1004	    which creates a new directory entry and fails with ``EEXIST`` when the
1005	    name is occupied by anything at all — a regular file, a directory or
1006	    a symlink, including one whose target does not exist.  A file another
1007	    program creates at the last instant — even an empty one or one
1008	    byte-identical to the package — is therefore never replaced, unlinked
1009	    or written through.  The package lives in the same directory as the
1010	    target, so the link is same-filesystem and a reader can only ever see
1011	    the complete file; this run's temporary link is removed afterwards,
1012	    leaving the occupant untouched on conflict.
1013	    """
1014	    _assert_target_name_free(target)
1015	    try:
1016	        os.link(temp_path, target)
1017	    except FileExistsError:
1018	        # The name was claimed in the gap after the check: link refused
1019	        # it atomically, so the occupant — file or symlink of any kind —
1020	        # is exactly as the other program left it.
1021	        raise ExportError(f"target already exists: {target}") from None
1022	    except OSError as error:
1023	        raise ExportError(f"cannot write export package: {error}") from error
1024	    # The target now carries the finished package under its own link.
1025	    # Drop the temporary link; if even that fails the package is already
1026	    # published, so the export still succeeds.
1027	    try:
1028	        os.unlink(temp_path)
1029	    except OSError:
1030	        pass

1033	def _write_package(
1034	    target: Path,
1035	    classes: dict[str, str],
1036	    members: list[dict[str, Any]],
1037	    manifest: dict[str, Any],
1038	    resolver: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]] | None = None,
1039	    source_anchor: _SourceAnchor | None = None,
1040	) -> None:
1041	    """Write the ZIP atomically: lock the target name, stream to a temp file.
1042	
1043	    The target is never overwritten: an occupied target is rejected both
1044	    when the export starts and once the package is finished, and the
1045	    finished package is claimed with a non-replacing ``link`` rather than
1046	    a rename, so a file or symlink (even a dangling one) that another
1047	    program creates while the images are copied is preserved and the
1048	    export fails naming the target.  Streaming to a temp file until the
1049	    whole package has been written, fsynced and source-verified means a
1050	    failure or interruption leaves neither an incomplete target nor this
1051	    run's temp file.  An flock on a lock file next to the target
1052	    serializes concurrent exports to the same path.
1053	    """
1054	    target = Path(target)
1055	    parent = target.parent
1056	    try:
1057	        parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1058	    except OSError as error:
1059	        raise ExportError(f"cannot create target directory {parent}: {error}") from error
1060	
1061	    lock_path = target.with_name(f".{target.name}.lock")
1062	    try:
1063	        lock_descriptor = os.open(lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
1064	    except OSError as error:
1065	        raise ExportError(f"cannot lock target {target}: {error}") from error
1066	
1067	    temp_path: Path | None = None
1068	    try:
1069	        fcntl.flock(lock_descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
1070	        _assert_target_name_free(target)
1071	
1072	        fd, temp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
1073	            prefix=f".{target.name}.", suffix=".tmp", dir=parent
1074	        )
1075	        temp_path = Path(temp_name)
1076	        try:
1077	            with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as stream:
1078	                _write_zip(
1079	                    stream,
1080	                    classes,
1081	                    members,
1082	                    manifest,
1083	                    resolver,
1084	                    source_anchor=source_anchor,
1085	                )
1086	                stream.flush()
1087	                os.fsync(stream.fileno())
1088	            if source_anchor is not None:
1089	                # Final gate before the package is published: every
1090	                # directory binding confirmed during the lookup must
1091	                # still hold.  A directory turned into a symlink while
1092	                # the last entry was streamed is caught here and the
1093	                # temp file is discarded rather than published.
1094	                source_anchor.verify_all()
1095	            # Claim the name only now that the package is complete and
1096	            # every source check passed; link refuses a name occupied at
1097	            # the last instant instead of replacing its occupant.
1098	            _publish_package(temp_path, target)
1099	            temp_path = None
1100	            _fsync_directory(parent)
1101	        except BaseException:
1102	            if temp_path is not None:
1103	                temp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
1104	            raise
1105	    except OSError as error:
1106	        raise ExportError(f"cannot write export package: {error}") from error
1107	    finally:
1108	        try:
1109	            fcntl.flock(lock_descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
1110	        finally:
1111	            os.close(lock_descriptor)

1151	def _write_sample(
1152	    archive: zipfile.ZipFile,
1153	    arc_name: str,
1154	    member: dict[str, Any],
1155	    resolver: Resolver | None = None,
1156	    source_anchor: _SourceAnchor | None = None,
1157	) -> None:
1158	    digest = member["sha256"]
1159	    hasher = hashlib.sha256()
1160	    if resolver is not None:
1161	        # Source-directory export: read from the matched copy only.  The
1162	        # plan's recorded source path is deliberately not consulted, so a
1163	        # still-usable original location cannot paper over a missing
1164	        # match.  First prove every ancestor directory is still the
1165	        # directory confirmed during the lookup (anchored to descriptors,
1166	        # not path strings), so a real directory replaced by a symlink
1167	        # after the lookup cannot lead to the bytes below.  The opened
1168	        # file itself is then pinned to the regular inode confirmed at
1169	        # lookup time, so a file swap after that confirmation cannot be
1170	        # copied in its place.
1171	        try:
1172	            source, expected_device, expected_inode = resolver[digest]
1173	        except KeyError:
1174	            raise ExportError(
1175	                f"sample {digest} in set {member['set']}: no file with "
1176	                f"matching content found under the source directory"
1177	            ) from None
1178	        if source_anchor is not None:

1181	            source, digest, expected_device, expected_inode
1182	        )

1188	    # and the classic local file header cannot describe a 2 GiB-or-larger
1189	    # entry, so decide the ZIP64 format up front from the confirmed file
1190	    # size (with the same 5% headroom zipfile itself uses, which also
1191	    # covers deflate growth on incompressible data).  Smaller entries open
1192	    # without ZIP64, keeping their archive bytes byte-identical to the
1193	    # classic format.  The size is only a format decision: the bytes
1194	    # actually read are always hash-verified below.
1195	    info = _file_info(arc_name)
1196	    info.file_size = source_size
1197	    force_zip64 = _entry_needs_zip64(source_size)
1198	    try:
1199	        with source_stream, archive.open(info, "w", force_zip64=force_zip64) as target_stream:
1200	            while True:
1201	                chunk = source_stream.read(_CHUNK_SIZE)
1202	                if not chunk:

1207	        raise ExportError(f"sample {digest}: cannot read source file {source}: {error}") from error

1213	        raise ExportError(

1215	            f"being read and is now too large to describe in the planned "
1216	            f"entry: {error}"
1217	        ) from error

1219	    actual = hasher.hexdigest()
1220	    if actual != digest:
1221	        raise ExportError(
1222	            f"sample {digest}: source file content changed or is corrupt "
1223	            f"while reading {source}: expected digest {digest}, got {actual}"
1224	        )

1230	    """Open the plan-recorded source, pinned to one confirmed regular file.
1231	
1232	    The export reads the sample bytes from the path saved in the plan.
1233	    That path may be a symbolic link when the export starts; as for
1234	    single-file import the link is followed once and the actual file it
1235	    names at that moment is the object confirmed for this read.  From
1236	    that point on the read is pinned with the same
1237	    inspect/open-no-follow/fstat-prove rule as a source-directory copy:
1238

1240	    * it is opened with ``O_NOFOLLOW`` and ``O_NONBLOCK``, so a name
1241	      swapped in the gap — a symlink or a named pipe with no writer —
1242	      can neither redirect nor block the open;

1244	      inspection named, so another regular file renamed onto the path in
1245	      that gap — even one with identical content, size and modification
1246	      time — is rejected rather than read, and a named pipe or other
1247	      non-regular object is rejected before any byte is waited on.

1251	    streaming, so large sources are still read in fixed chunks.

1295	    if stat.S_ISCHR(mode):
1296	        return "character device"
1297	    if stat.S_ISBLK(mode):

1310	    “not a regular file” wording (optionally naming what it is).  An

1312	    inspection and the proved open — another regular file, even a

1314	    without blocking — says the recorded source was replaced before it
1315	    was read, naming what sits there now.  Underlying access failures
1316	    keep their ``OSError`` text.

1330	        if kind == "regular file":
1331	            detail = "now names a different regular file than the one confirmed"

1340	        confirmed.ConfirmStage.OPEN: "open",
1341	        confirmed.ConfirmStage.PROVE: "read",
